questions.stem: Why can convection NOT occur in solids?

options.text: Solids are too hot for convection
Particles in solids are fixed in position and cannot flow to form convection currents
Solids do not contain any particles
Solids are always at the same temperature throughout

questions.explanation: Convection requires particles to physically move and circulate. In solids, particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces, so they cannot flow. Convection can only occur in fluids (liquids and gases) where particles are free to move.
